parts.latex:
The five-number summary of a dataset is given.

Lowest score $= 1$

Lower quartile $(Q_1) = 4$

Median $(Q_2) = 7$

Upper quartile $(Q_3) = 10$

Highest score $= 20$

Is 20 an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.

solutions.latex:
A score is an outlier if it lies above $Q_3+1.5\times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= Q_3-Q_1 \\ &= 10-4 \\ &= 6 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Upper fence} &= Q_3+1.5\times IQR \\ &= 10+1.5\times 6 \\ &= 19 \end{aligned}$$
Since $20>19$, the highest score is above the upper fence.
$$\therefore\ \text{20 is an outlier}$$
criteria: Finds the upper fence, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Calculate the mean and the range of goals that Sophie scored throughout the season.
Use calculations to determine whether any of Sophie's scores are outliers.

criteria: Correct mean or correct range, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The quartiles of the data are
$$Q_1 = 5, \quad Q_3 = 11$$
so the interquartile range is
$$IQR = 11 - 5 = 6$$
Outliers lie below $Q_1 - 1.5\times IQR$ or above $Q_3 + 1.5\times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 - 1.5\times IQR &= 5 - 1.5\times 6 = -4 \\ Q_3 + 1.5\times IQR &= 11 + 1.5\times 6 = 20 \end{aligned}$$
Since $24 > 20$, 24 is an outlier.
criteria: Finds the outlier boundaries $-4$ and $20$, or equivalent merit
